gaps: Auth token must be captured manually from browser DevTools -- the OAuth2 client_credentials token-mint endpoint was not isolated during discovery (fires before any capture hook attaches). See auth_narrative.

Travel-agency code validation path is unconfirmed -- only corporate and group-attendee code paths were verified live; the guessed travel-agency path segment returned UNSUPPORTED_CODE_TYPE and was not implemented.
The successful (valid-code) response shape for codes validate-* is unconfirmed -- only the invalid/404 error shape was observed live since no real valid code was available to test.

novel_features.name: Multi-hotel rate compare
novel_features.description: Check several boutique hotels for the same dates in one call, ranked by lowest fee-inclusive total.
novel_features.rationale: Each TravelClick hotel's widget only knows about itself -- comparing properties today means opening one browser tab per hotel.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user names more than one property for the same trip instead of calling 'rates search' repeatedly.

novel_features.name: Cheapest night across saved hotels
novel_features.description: Scan several hotels' calendars at once and return the single best hotel+date combination.
novel_features.rationale: No widget or competitor offers a cross-property calendar since each hotel's booking page only exposes its own.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user is flexible on both hotel and date, not just date.

novel_features.name: Saved hotel aliases
novel_features.description: Give a memorable name to a TravelClick hotel ID instead of memorizing a 6-digit number.
novel_features.rationale: Hotel IDs only exist as an opaque query-string value on the booking URL; nothing else names them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before repeated lookups against the same property so later commands can take the alias instead of the raw ID.

novel_features.name: Rate-snapshot price-drift history
novel_features.description: Track how a hotel's rates move over time from your own saved search history.
novel_features.rationale: Neither the widget nor any CRS surface exposes historical pricing -- it only exists if you capture it yourself.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this after the user has run a few 'rates search --save' calls and wants to know if a rate went up or down.

novel_features.name: Rate-code check across saved hotels
novel_features.description: Test one corporate or group code against every saved hotel at once.
novel_features.rationale: A client or event code is often valid chain- or event-wide, but the widget only lets you test one hotel at a time.
novel_features.example: travelclick-pp-cli codes check-all ACME2026 --type corporate --hotels made-nyc,<alias2>
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user has a code but isn't sure which of their saved hotels honors it.

narrative.headline: Search any TravelClick-powered hotel's own rates directly -- room types, rate plans, fee-inclusive pricing, and the cheapest night to book -- without opening a browser tab per property.
narrative.value_prop: TravelClick/iHotelier powers the direct-booking widget for thousands of independent and boutique hotels. This CLI calls the same JSON API the widget itself uses to search availability, scan a date range for the lowest rate, validate corporate/group codes, and compare several hotels side by side. Search and info only -- no reservation, no guest PII, no payment data ever touches it.
narrative.auth_narrative: TravelClick's widget mints a short-lived (~1 hour) OAuth2 client_credentials Bearer token client-side during page load. The exact token-mint endpoint was not isolated during discovery (it fires before any capture hook can attach), so this CLI cannot mint its own token yet -- capture one manually: open the hotel's booking page in Chrome, open DevTools' Network tab, filter for api.travelclick.com, click any request, and copy the Authorization header's value (everything after 'Bearer ') into TRAVELCLICK_TOKEN. Re-capture roughly every hour.

quickstart.comment: Health check that works without a token.
Look up Made Hotel NYC's profile, policies, and fees once TRAVELCLICK_TOKEN is set.
Search room types and rate plans for specific dates.
Scan two months for the cheapest night before committing to dates.
Save a memorable name for the hotel ID.

troubleshoots.fix: TRAVELCLICK_TOKEN has expired (~1 hour TTL) -- re-capture it from DevTools per the auth instructions above.
The code isn't recognized by this specific hotel -- corporate/group codes are hotel-specific, not chain-wide. Try 'codes check-all' across your saved hotels instead.

troubleshoots.symptom: rates calendar returns fewer days than requested
troubleshoots.fix: TravelClick truncates a multi-room calendar scan to roughly 60 days -- split a longer range into two calls.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when checking a specific independent or boutique hotel's own direct rates -- price-matching against an OTA, finding the cheapest date for a stay, validating a corporate or event code, or comparing a handful of TravelClick-powered properties for the same trip.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to make or modify a reservation -- it is search/info only and has no booking command by design.
Do not use this CLI for hotels that don't use TravelClick/iHotelier as their booking engine -- check that the hotel's booking URL is bookings.travelclick.com first.
Do not use this CLI to look up a guest's existing reservation, loyalty account, or payment details -- those require guest login and are out of scope.

recipes.title: Cheapest room+rate for a stay
recipes.explanation: Narrows the deeply-nested avail response to just room name, rate, and rate code per plan instead of the full policy/amenity/image payload.

recipes.title: Find the cheapest night in a month
recipes.explanation: Returns the lowest rate for every day in the range so you can sort for the minimum.

recipes.title: Check a corporate code before searching
recipes.explanation: Confirms a rate-access code is live for this hotel before building a search around it.

recipes.title: Compare three boutique hotels for the same weekend
recipes.explanation: Fans out the search across hotels and ranks them by lowest fee-inclusive total.
